title: Cosanima repo split: monorepo → core + six frontend repos
goal: Split the monorepo into the cosanima core (Rust ingestor + CLI + tool suite + agents) plus six independently versioned and CI'd frontend repos (cosanima-go/java/cpp/rust/ts/csharp), promoting the JSONL schema and FQN rules into a versioned cross-repo contract.

title: Core repo scope defined
body: The core repo keeps the Rust ingestor + CLI (all of src/*.rs incl. main.rs, ingest.rs, load.rs, schema.rs, graph.rs, classify.rs, cleanup.rs, artifacts.rs, specs.rs, spec_cmd.rs, plan_cmd.rs, review_cmd.rs), build.rs, the single-sourced .opencode tool suite + agents, and the distribution surface (Formula, install.sh). It no longer carries any scanner frontend source.

title: JSONL schema + FQN rules → versioned contract
body: The unified JSONL schema (schema.rs: Record/edge records) and the FQN rules are promoted from internal code to a versioned cross-repo contract with its own revision, so frontend repos and the core agree on the format. This is the seed of the versioned handshake specced in cosanima-frontend-interface.

title: build.rs orchestration changes form
body: The monorepo's build.rs orchestration (which compiles all six frontends and stages them to target/<profile>/frontends) changes form: the core no longer builds frontends in-tree. Local dev installs frontends via brew (or the curl installer) or uses a dev harness; the compile-time baked frontend paths in src/main.rs (frontend_cmd/available_languages) are reworked for the split layout.

summary: Split the monorepo into cosanima core + six frontend repos (source 'Split monorepo into carto ... plus six frontend repos'): each frontend is its own language/toolchain with its own build pipeline, so it gets its own repo, native CI, own versioning, and own contributors.

The split forces a stable frontend interface: the JSONL schema + FQN rules are promoted to a versioned cross-repo contract (the two halves — conformance mode + runtime assessment — are specced in cosanima-frontend-interface).

body: No behavioural change to any frontend during the split: it is a pure relocation + packaging change; fidelity stays as-is (C++ heuristic, Go/Java/Rust/TS/C# exact).

No new frontend languages beyond the existing six, and no change to the unified JSONL schema *content* within the split itself — only its promotion to a versioned contract (revisioning is cosanima-frontend-interface).
No Windows build-out of frontends as part of the split (platform stance is ruled by the parent stable-surface requirement).

source: SPEC-1.0.0.md named the core `carto` and the six frontend repos `carto-go/java/cpp/rust/ts/csharp`, and asked `carto-1.0?` for the parent; materialized with the binding name: cosanima core + cosanima-go/java/cpp/rust/ts/csharp, parent cosanima-1.0 [with user].

Graph-coverage caveat: the six frontend dirs exist on disk (src/golib, javalib, cpplib, rustlib, tslib, csharplib) and four have scanned code nodes (go/cpp/csharp/java); the ts module node has no scanned children and src/rustlib is not in the graph, so anchors reflect scanned coverage only — the split still moves all six dirs.
Seven repos exist under the cosanima org; the core repo contains no scanner frontend source and each frontend repo contains its own frontend + native build.
The JSONL schema + FQN rules exist as a versioned cross-repo contract document with a revision identifier, referenced by the core and all six frontends.
A developer can build the core, install a frontend via brew/harness, and `cosanima scan` a repo of that language end-to-end without in-tree frontend sources.
Verification: clone each frontend repo fresh, run its native build + scan, and confirm the output JSONL validates against the published contract revision.

title: Six frontend repos created
body: Each of the six frontends moves to its own repo under the really-knows-ai GitHub org with native versioning and its own contributors: really-knows-ai/cosanima-go (src/golib), really-knows-ai/cosanima-java (src/javalib), really-knows-ai/cosanima-cpp (src/cpplib), really-knows-ai/cosanima-rust (src/rustlib), really-knows-ai/cosanima-ts (src/tslib), really-knows-ai/cosanima-csharp (src/csharplib). Code is relocated without behavioural change; the frontend repos own their build pipelines, releases, and CI (CI detail in cosanima-frontend-ci). Graph note: go/cpp/csharp/java frontends have scanned nodes (anchored); ts has only a module node and rustlib is not scanned — anchors reflect scanned coverage only.

title: Dev harness + local frontend install
body: A dev harness + local frontend install path replaces in-tree build orchestration: developers install frontends locally (brew install really-knows-ai/cosanima/cosanima-<lang>) or via a harness, and `cosanima scan` resolves them through COSANIMA_FRONTEND_DIR / the installed-frontends directory (reworking apg.frontend_dir / frontend_cmd in src/main.rs).

title: Seven-repo org ready for flag-day
body: The seven repos — really-knows-ai/cosanima (core) + really-knows-ai/cosanima-go/java/cpp/rust/ts/csharp (six frontends) — are created under the really-knows-ai org with CI enabled and docs ported, ready for the coordinated v1.0.0 flag-day (tags/release are gated by the parent cosanima-1.0 spec).

summary: Owning GitHub org is `really-knows-ai`, not `cosanima`: the seven repos are really-knows-ai/cosanima (core) + really-knows-ai/cosanima-{go,java,cpp,rust,ts,csharp} and the brew tap lives under the same org. The product name stays cosanima, so the operative availability criterion is the cosanima* repo names being free under really-knows-ai, not a GitHub org literally named cosanima [with user].

title: Shallow split executed (no full history rehome)
body: The split is SHALLOW: each frontend moves to its own repo WITHOUT rehoming its full per-directory git history. Provenance is not preserved via git filter-repo/subtree — each frontend repo starts from the current code state (history can be referenced but not fully rehomed); the core keeps the monorepo history. (User's binding ruling replaces the earlier full-rehome assumption.)

summary: History rehome → SHALLOW split (user's binding ruling, replacing the earlier [autonomous] full-rehome ruling): frontends move to their own repos without rehoming full per-directory git history — the split starts each frontend repo from the current code state; provenance is not preserved via git filter-repo/subtree (history can be referenced, not fully rehomed); the core keeps the monorepo history [with user].

body: The split is shallow: each frontend repo starts from the current code state with no full per-directory history rehome; per-directory commit provenance is not carried over via filter-repo/subtree (the core keeps the monorepo history).

Verification: cloning a frontend repo shows a shallow history starting from the split's current code state (no full pre-split per-directory commit set); a README/pointer in each frontend repo references the original monorepo history.
